text:
maria.g: Quick sync — I want to lock down the load-sweep we run for kernel selection experiments. We keep mixing replay and synth and I'm worried the TTFT/TPOT defs we're using aren't apples-to-apples.

nate.k: Agreed. Can you call out exactly where our diffs are? e.g. sampling, kv-warm, batching windows?

maria.g: Yep. Quick list: 1) replay traffic has varying context lengths -> affects KV hit rate. 2) synthetic uses fixed seq len -> better batching density. 3) we currently measure TTFT from incoming request to first token emitted, but sometimes bench harness timestamps at post-routing enqueue.

ryan.t: That enqueue vs ingress timestamp has bitten us before. For TTFT we should start timer at request _arrival_ at the runtime entrypoint (pre-routing) so routing/cold-load is counted.

jen.li: +1. Also call out TPOT: how are we defining it? I thought TPOT = total processing time per token including kernel execution + memcpy + kernel overhead?

maria.g: For our purposes TPOT = end-to-end per-token compute time on the selected device (so includes kernel exec + device <-> host copies for models that do that) but excludes queuing/wait time. We'll report both TPOT and queue wait separately.

samir: What about p95/p99 reporting? For goodput we used tokens emitted per second when KV hit ratio above X. That felt hand-wavy.

nate.k: Proposal: report these metrics for each test run: - TTFT (start=ingress, first token out) - TPOT (median & p95 kernel-only) - Queue wait distribution (p50/p95/p99) - Goodput (tokens/sec delivered to clients) - QPS (requests/sec attempted). Also annotate KV hit rate and batching factor.

ryan.t: Sounds solid. We should also separate warmup phase where KV cache is populated. Suggest: 5 min warmup (replay) then measurement window 10 min. For synthetic sweeps we run 2 min warmup then measure 6 min.

jen.li: Can we add an automated check for kernel flips? Last run flipped from fused-attn to attn-x and we saw a TPOT regression but goodput was flat — probably batching interaction. Need the profiler traces aligned to kernel selection timestamps.

maria.g: Agreed. Dev plan: - include kernel-selection log lines in harness output (format: KERNEL_CHOICE ts kernel_name heuristic). - capture perf counters per kernel call (latency micros, occupancy). - upload sample flamegraph for a subset of requests.

samir: Example log snippet we can parse:
```
KERNEL_CHOICE 2198765490 fused_attn heuristic=batch_size=8,seq=512
KERNEL_CALL 2198765490 fused_attn latency_us=432 memcpy_us=12
KVCACHE_HIT 2198765491 true key_len=64
```

nate.k: Nice. Also record batching_factor: number_of_requests_in_batch per step. That explains why TPOT might increase while throughput stable.

maria.g: For apples-to-apples between replay and synthetic: 1) fix seq length distribution in synth to match replay percentiles (p50/p90/p99). 2) seed synth KV keys from replay trace so hit rates match. 3) use same ingress timestamping method.

ryan.t: Implementation note: our replay harness already exports seq_percentiles.json. We'll add a synth generator that accepts that as input.

jen.li: Regression detection: if TPOT_med increases by >10% or p95 TPOT increases >20% while goodput drops <5% (i.e., compute got worse but throughput same), flag for kernel-selection review.

samir: I like that rule. Add a separate alert if queue wait p95 increases >30% (indicates batching collapse or slowdown).

maria.g: I'll put this into a short SOP. Draft checklist: 
- Pre-reqs: workload trace + seq_percentiles.json
- Warmup: replay 5m or synth warmup matching kv hit rate
- Sweep: run kernels under test with identical ingress timing for 3 seeds
- Capture: kernel logs, perf samples, batching histogram, kv hit metrics
- Metrics: TTFT, TPOT (med/p95/p99), goodput, QPS, queue wait (p50/p95/p99), batch_factor, kv_hit_rate
- Regression rules: (as jen/ samir suggested)

nate.k: Can you commit the SOP to bench-playbooks and add a sample CI job? bench-bot: please remind us to attach an example trace when we run this. :slightly_smiling_face:

bench-bot: Reminder queued: attach a representative trace + seq_percentiles.json for any kernel selection PR.

maria.g: I'll write the SOP and a small harness diff. Target PR by EOD tomorrow. If anyone wants to add checks or thresholds, drop comments here.

ryan.t: I'll add a flamegraph collector that samples 1 in 100 requests.

jen.li: I'll write the regression alert rules into the dashboard.

samir: Ping me when the parser for KERNEL_CHOICE lines is in, I will add KV-hit breakdown in the report.

maria.g: Thanks all. Quick follow-up: do we want to include TPOT normalized by batch_size to make cross-batch comparisons easier?

nate.k: Yes — report TPOT_per_token = TPOT / effective_batch_size as a derived metric. That should reduce confusion.

maria.g: Great. Closing thread, will post PR link here when ready. :rocket:
